# UByte <img class="product" src="media/bl-20x14.png" alt="BlitzLLVM" title="BlitzLLVM" width="20" height="14">

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [Language Features](Language-Features) · [Types](Language-Features-Types)

</div>


```blitzbasic
UByte(value)
UByte:UInt8(value)
```

**Returns:** The UByte.

## Description

<img class="product" src="media/bl-20x14.png" alt="BlitzLLVM" title="BlitzLLVM" width="20" height="14"> This command does not exist in the original Blitz products. BlitzLLVM adds it.

<!-- AUTOGENERATED COPYRIGHT HEADER START -->
Converts a number or a text to a UByte, an 8-bit integer from 0 to 255. This is a BlitzLLVM extension: the originals only know `Int` and `Float`. A whole number that is too large or below 0 keeps its lowest 8 bits (`UByte(-1)` is 255), a real is rounded to the nearest whole number (halves go to the even one) and stops at 0 or 255 if it is outside. Use [SatUByte](SatUByte) to stop whole numbers at 0 and 255 as well.

## Differences

* Not in the originals, which have no integers of other sizes.

## Examples

```blitzbasic
Print UByte(200)
Print UByte(-1)
Print UByte(256)
Print UByte(300.0)
```

```text
200
255
0
255
```
